origin: hand-built from SPEC.md v4.1 §9.1 + §13.2; clauses and CHANGELOG entries browser-verified 2026-08-30
invariant: §9.1 requires decoders to accept the legacy root form [0]: as an empty array — a decoder MUST since CHANGELOG [3.1], tested here directly rather than through any encoder. The encoder prohibition that makes it unreachable from a round-trip is NEWER than the decoder obligation: [3.1] made emitting the canonical form a SHOULD, and only [4.1] made the legacy form MUST NOT be emitted. So the case is unreachable through a 4.1-conforming encoder specifically; a conforming 3.x encoder could legitimately have produced this wire
refs: SPEC.md v4.1 §9.1 Decoding: decoders MUST accept key: [], [], and the legacy forms key[0<delim?>]: and [0<delim?>]:
SPEC.md v4.1 §13.2 decoder checklist: accept empty arrays in both forms
SPEC.md v4.1 §9.1 Encoding (root position): encoders MUST emit [] on its own line; the legacy [0<delim?>]: form MUST NOT be emitted — this half dates from [4.1], not [3.1]
CHANGELOG [3.1] 2026-05-18: decoders MUST accept both canonical and legacy forms, encoders SHOULD emit the canonical form — the two halves differ in normative strength
CHANGELOG [4.1] 2026-07-26: encoders lost their remaining latitude over form; empty arrays emit key: [] and [], never the legacy key[0]:

MECHANISM: [0]: is a valid root array header (§6 length production admits the single digit 0), so §5 root-form discovery takes its FIRST branch (valid root array header -> decode a root array) rather than the []-literal branch, and length 0 with no inline content yields the empty array. A decoder that fails this case will therefore most likely raise a header-parse or count error, not an empty-array error

OBSERVED 2026-08-30 (frozen env): ALL THREE decoders accept [0]: — no divergence. The same run shows python decoding the CANONICAL [] as the string "[]" and rust ERRORING on it (seeds/002), so both accept the legacy form and fail the canonical one: the legacy form is the BETTER-supported one, the opposite of what this case was authored expecting

WHAT THIS CASE ESTABLISHED WITHOUT DIVERGING: seeds/002 renders rust as 'behind the rule, not violating it (claims spec 3.0)', which was pure version arithmetic. This case supplies the evidence — rust genuinely implements the pre-3.1 world, accepting the only form that existed then. It also bounds toon-python#61 to the canonical form alone rather than empty arrays generally
